outcome: Give plant manager / operations excellence director a governed method to improve unplanned bottleneck downtime hours using PLC alarms, vibration traces and maintenance orders, with final decisions…
overview: Predictive Maintenance of Bottleneck Machines addresses teams rely on lagging aggregates when forecasts or decisions depend on changing operational conditions in manufacturing operations. The first proof of value uses PLC alarms, vibration traces and maintenance orders. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is unplanned bottleneck downtime hours, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: PLC alarms, vibration traces and maintenance orders; define unplanned bottleneck downtime hours and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Plant Manager / Operations Excellence Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including backtest across seasonal and peak periods with a holdout cohort.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for unplanned bottleneck downtime hours
